page: Amazon Web Services c8i.96xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 384 vCPUs and 192 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The system includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, with read-only cached speeds reaching 30,590.21 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which contribute to top-tier performance in Passmark extended instructions and encryption tests.

While multi-threaded capabilities and prompt processing for large language models rank in the top tier, single-core performance is average. Text generation speeds for LLM inference represent a notable bottleneck, falling into the average to poor categories. This resource profile, characterized by high compute density and fast DDR5 memory but no local storage, is suited for highly parallelized workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression.
